summary: Nani Gopal Majumdar was an Indian archaeology and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1916–1920) and served as Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India (1931) and the Indian Museum's Archæological Section (~1932–1938).
Nantu Shaw works in philosophy and Indology. Shaw studied as a Visiting Scholar at Stony Brook University under doctoral supervisor Sthaneshwar Timalsina (attested 2026).

Naoji Okuyama is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. After completing doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1980–1985), he worked there as an assistant and lecturer (~1985–1991) before becoming a professor at Koyasan University (~1998; attested 2026).
Naoki Kano was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1890–1893). He held a post at Kyoto University from 1906 and taught Taichiro Kobayashi.
Naoki Nabeshima is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Attested in 2004, he founded Ryukoku University and served there as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies.

Naoko Nishimura is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She earned her PhD at Tohoku University by 2002, studying under Toshifumi Goto (attested 2012), and served there as a researcher (attested 2012) and professor (attested 2026).

Naomi Appleton is a Buddhist, Indology, and religious studies scholar. She earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under supervisors Christopher Minkowski and David Gellner. She was a fellow at Cardiff University and serves as Professor and Co-Director at Edinburgh.

Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Tokyo and Oxford under Takakusu, Macdonell, Geldner, and Lévi. He held Tokyo's Chair of Sanskrit (1942–1960) and directed the Toyo Bunko (1974).
Naoya Funahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts as a research fellow at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and at Otani University (attested 1981).

Narada Maha Thera was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St. Benedict's College, Ceylon University College, and under Pelene Siri Vajiragnana (~1916). He served as Superior at Vajiraramaya (~1955–1983) and taught Ayya Khema and Sīlaratano.

Narayan Hemandas Samtani is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD (1957–1961) and held a research fellowship at the University of Delhi, later serving as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (~1961).
Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya was a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Calcutta from approximately 1967 to 1999.

Nariaki Nakazato is an Indologist and historian. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1977) and Calcutta (PhD 1979–1985). He held posts at Toyo Bunko, CEACS, Kobe University, and served as Professor at Tokyo (1984–2010).
Narimoto Tamayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held a post as professor at Taisho University (attested 1974 and 1988).
Natalie Gummer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She held a post at Harvard University (attested 2001) and was appointed professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

Natalie Maxwell is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied under Geshe Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Lengden, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota, completing her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1975) under Stephan Beyer.
Natalie Rothman is a historian. She completed her studies at the University of Michigan (1999–2006) and took up a post at the University of Toronto in 2006.

Natasha Heller is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard (2005), held posts at UC Berkeley and UCLA, and joined the faculty at the University of Virginia (attested 2026).

Natasha Reichle works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley, where she studied under Joanna Gottfried Williams, Amin Sweeney, Lewis Lancaster, Patricia Berger, and Jeffrey Alan Hadler.
Natasja Bosma is an Indology scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Groningen (~2013–2018) under the doctoral supervision of Hans T. Bakker.
